name: Subang Airport Regeneration Plan (SARP)
status_detail: Construction · Phase One terminal expansion under way; narrowbody jet services resumed June 2024
summary: The cabinet-approved plan to turn Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport, Kuala Lumpur's main airport until 1998, back into a commercial air hub: expanded terminal, new narrowbody parking bays and the return of Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 jets after 26 years.

scale.label: Passenger capacity
scale.value: 1.5 million to 3 million pax a year in Phase One; up to 8 million by Phase Three

scale.label: Phase One airside
scale.value: Up to 5 narrowbody bays and 6 turboprop bays

why_it_matters: The only airport in the Klang Valley that can add capacity inside the already-built-up city. A working city airport plus the surrounding aerospace ecosystem changes the development math for Subang, Shah Alam and Petaling, and it is the second half of Malaysia Airports' Aeropolis strategy alongside KLIA.
questions_to_follow: Which airlines actually commit scheduled jet services to Subang?
When does Phase One complete, and what triggers the 8-million-passenger Phase Three?
location_precision: Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport site, Subang. Coordinates from the airport's Wikipedia page.
